introduction.zh: 门板被斧头劈开一个洞，医生钻进去，屋里却没有窗，只有贴着墙的大木桶、挂着的锡壶和一股酒味。他划亮一根火柴，往地上一照——这间锁着的小屋里，好像不只有木桶。
introduction.en: An axe is found, and the Doctor cuts a hole in a locked door. Inside there is no window, only barrels, pewter jugs and a smell of wine. He strikes a match and looks down at the floor. What is waiting in the dark little room?

sentences: 马上就找到了一把斧头。
医生很快在门上砍出一个洞，大得足够人钻进去。
起初他什么也看不见，里面太黑了。
于是他划着了一根火柴。
房间很小；没有窗户；天花板很低。
家具只有一张小凳子。
房间四周靠墙立着大木桶，桶底都固定住，免得船身一摇晃就倒下来；木桶上方，木钉上挂着大大小小的锡壶。
空气里有一股很浓的酒味。
地板正中坐着一个约莫八岁的小男孩，哭得很伤心。
「我说，这是海盗的朗姆酒舱！」吉普压低声音说。

hints.zh: 朗姆酒舱，船上存放朗姆酒的储藏室。
hints.en: The rum-room: the store-room on a ship where the rum is kept.

hints.zh: 感叹语，「我说」「真是的」，用来表示惊讶。
hints.en: An old exclamation of surprise: “Well, I must say!”

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

sentences: 「是啊。
真够『朗姆』的！」咕咕说。
「这味儿熏得我头晕。」

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s pig.

hints.zh: 咕咕没听懂：rum 既是「朗姆酒」，也是英国旧口语里的「古怪」，他顺着酒味说「太朗姆了」。
hints.en: Gub-Gub misses the joke: rum is the drink, but in old slang it also means “odd”, so he says “very rum”.

sentences: 小男孩发现面前站着一个男人，还有那么多动物从破门洞里朝里看，显得相当害怕。
可火柴的光一照见约翰·杜立德的脸，他立刻不哭了，站起身来。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，医生的全名。
hints.en: John Dolittle: the Doctor’s full name.

quiz.question: What does Jip think the little room is?
options: The pirates’ rum-room
The ship’s kitchen
A store-room for sails

feedback.zh: 吉普一闻那酒味就说：「这是海盗的朗姆酒舱！」咕咕还跟着用 rum 这个词开玩笑。
feedback.en: Jip smells the wine and whispers that it is the pirates’ rum-room; Gub-Gub then makes a joke on the word rum.

quiz.question: What is the little boy doing when the Doctor first sees him?
options: Sitting on the floor and crying
Sleeping on the little stool
Hiding behind the barrels

feedback.zh: 火柴一亮，只见地板正中坐着一个八岁上下的男孩，哭得很伤心；凳子空着，桶边也没人躲着。
feedback.en: By the light of the match the Doctor sees a boy of about eight sitting in the middle of the floor, crying bitterly.

grammar.excerpt: For furniture there was only one little stool

focus.zh: For furniture 提到句首，先说「家具」这一项；真正的结构是 there was + 单数名词。
focus.en: For furniture is pulled to the front to name the topic; the real pattern is there was + a singular noun.

introduction.zh: 男孩先问一句：你不是海盗吧？然后说起前天的事——他和舅舅在海上打鱼，被海盗抓上了这条船。海盗要舅舅入伙，舅舅死活不肯。可第二天，男孩在船上再也找不到他了。
introduction.en: The boy asks the Doctor a nervous question: is he one of the pirates? Then he tells what happened two days ago. He and his uncle were fishing when the pirates caught them. They wanted the uncle to join them, and he said no. Next morning the uncle was gone.

sentences: 「你不是海盗吧？」他问。
医生仰起头，放声大笑；小男孩也笑了，走过来拉住他的手。
「你笑起来像个朋友，」他说，「不像海盗。
你能告诉我我舅舅在哪儿吗？」
「恐怕不行，」医生说。
「你最后一次见到他是什么时候？」
「是前天，」男孩说。
「我和舅舅坐我们的小船出海打鱼，海盗来了，把我们抓住了。
他们弄沉了我们的渔船，把我们两个都带到了这条船上。
他们说想让我舅舅跟他们一样当海盗——因为他在什么天气里都能把船驶得很好。
可他说他不想当海盗，因为杀人抢东西不是好渔夫干的活儿。
于是头子本·阿里非常恼火，牙齿咬得咯咯响，说要是舅舅不照他们说的做，就把他扔进海里。
他们把我打发到下面去；我听见上面有打斗的声音。
第二天他们让我上来时，舅舅却哪儿都看不见了。
我问海盗他在哪儿，可他们不肯告诉我。
我很怕他们把他扔进海里，淹死了。」

hints.zh: sink 的过去式，这里是口语说法：弄沉、使船下沉。
hints.en: A colloquial past form of sink: they sank our boat.

hints.zh: 在各种天气里，不管风浪好坏。
hints.en: In all weathers: in every kind of weather, good or bad.

hints.zh: 本·阿里，这伙海盗的头子。
hints.en: Ben Ali, the leader of the pirates.

hints.zh: 咬牙切齿，气得直磨牙。
hints.en: Gnashed his teeth: he ground his teeth in anger.

hints.zh: 哪儿都看不见，人影也没有。
hints.en: Nowhere to be seen: he could not be found anywhere.

quiz.question: Why does Ben Ali get angry with the boy’s uncle?
options: The uncle refuses to be a pirate
The uncle cannot sail in bad weather
The uncle has taken the pirates’ boat

feedback.zh: 舅舅说杀人抢东西不是好渔夫干的活儿，不肯入伙，本·阿里才发火，威胁把他扔下海。
feedback.en: The uncle had just said that killing and stealing was no work for a good fisherman, so Ben Ali lost his temper.

quiz.question: What does the boy fear has happened to his uncle?
options: The pirates threw him into the sea
He is locked in another room
He has sailed home without him

feedback.zh: 男孩最后说，他很怕海盗把舅舅扔进海里淹死了——这只是他的猜测，他并没有亲眼看见。
feedback.en: The boy ends by saying he is very much afraid they threw his uncle into the sea and drowned him.

grammar.excerpt: You aren’t one of the pirates, are you?

focus.zh: 前句是否定的 aren’t，后面就换成肯定的 are you；男孩用来说出自己的猜测，等医生点头。
focus.en: The statement is negative (aren’t), so the tag turns positive (are you): the boy is guessing and wants to be told he is right.

introduction.zh: 男孩又哭了。医生没有追问，先带他去餐厅喝茶，桌上还有草莓酱。动物们围在一边听着，鸭子凑到医生椅背后，小声出了一个主意——这主意跟海里的动物有关。它真能问出答案吗？
introduction.en: The boy starts crying again. The Doctor does not push him; he takes him to the dining-room for tea. All the animals stand around and listen. Then Dab-Dab leans behind the Doctor’s chair and whispers a strange idea about the animals of the sea. Could it work?

sentences: 小男孩又哭了起来。
「好了——等一等，」医生说。
「别哭。
我们去餐厅喝茶，一边喝一边商量。
也许你舅舅一直好好的呢。
你并不知道他淹死了，对吧？
这总算是一点安慰。
说不定我们能替你找到他。
我们先去喝茶——有草莓酱；然后再看能做些什么。」

hints.zh: 把事情谈一谈、商量清楚。
hints.en: Talk it over: to discuss it until things are clear.

sentences: 动物们一直围在旁边，非常好奇地听着。
他们进了船上的餐厅，正喝着茶，达布达布走到医生椅子后面，小声说起话来。

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

sentences: 「去问问海豚，那男孩的舅舅是不是淹死了——它们准知道。」

hints.zh: 海豚（鼠海豚），一种小型的鲸类，常成群在船边游。
hints.en: Porpoises: small sea animals like dolphins, often swimming in groups.

sentences: 「好哇，」医生说着，又拿起一块果酱面包。
「你舌头弄出的那种咔嗒咔嗒的怪声音是什么？」男孩问。
「哦，我只是用鸭子话说了两句，」医生回答。
「这是达布达布，我的宠物之一。」
「我连鸭子有语言都不知道，」男孩说。
「这些别的动物也都是你的宠物吗？
那个两个脑袋的怪东西是什么？」
「嘘！」医生小声说。
「那是『推我拉你』。
别让他看见我们在说他——他会羞得不得了的……
告诉我，你怎么会被关在那间小屋子里的？」

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那只两个脑袋的动物，医生从非洲带回来的。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu, the two-headed animal the Doctor brought from Africa.

hints.zh: come to be 是「怎么会落到……的地步」；这里在问男孩怎么被关进去的。
hints.en: Come to be means “happen to end up”: the Doctor asks how the boy ended up locked up.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor want them to do before they talk about the uncle?
options: Go and have tea in the dining-room
Search all the pirates’ rooms
Sail back to the boy’s village

feedback.zh: 医生先让孩子离开那间小屋：「我们去餐厅喝茶，一边喝一边商量。」还说有草莓酱。
feedback.en: The Doctor first says, “Let’s go and have tea in the dining-room, and we’ll talk it over.”

quiz.question: What does Dab-Dab whisper to the Doctor?
options: Ask the porpoises whether the uncle was drowned
Ask the boy to describe his uncle
Tell the boy that his uncle is safe

feedback.zh: 达布达布凑到椅背后说：去问海豚，它们准知道那男孩的舅舅有没有淹死。
feedback.en: Dab-Dab whispers that he should ask the porpoises: they will know whether the boy’s uncle was drowned.

grammar.excerpt: Let’s go and have tea in the dining-room

focus.zh: Let’s 把医生自己也算进去，等于「我们去吧」；go and have 两个动词直接相连，中间不用 to。
focus.en: Let’s includes the Doctor himself; go and have joins two verbs with and, not with to.

introduction.zh: 男孩说出舅舅的样子：一头很红的头发，胳膊上刺着一个锚，是南大西洋上最好的水手。医生记下了这些，也问清了船名。凭这几个记号，真能从茫茫大海上把一个人找出来吗？
introduction.en: The boy describes his uncle: very red hair, an anchor tattooed on his arm, the best sailor in the South Atlantic. The Doctor asks for the name of the boat too. Can a few marks like that really find one man on the sea?

sentences: 「海盗要去抢另一条船上的东西，就把我关在那儿了。
我听见有人砍门，不知道会是谁。
发现是你，我高兴极了。
你觉得你能帮我找到舅舅吗？」
「我们会拼命去试的，」医生说。
「那你舅舅长什么样？」
「他有一头红头发，」男孩回答，「很红的头发，胳膊上还刺着一个锚。
他力气大，是个好舅舅，也是南大西洋上最好的水手。
他的渔船叫『俏莎莉号』——一条单桅纵帆船。」

hints.zh: 南大西洋。
hints.en: The South Atlantic: the southern part of the Atlantic Ocean.

hints.zh: 「俏莎莉号」，舅舅那条渔船的名字。
hints.en: The Saucy Sally: the name of the uncle’s fishing-boat.

hints.zh: 帆船术语：cutter 是一种单桅纵帆的帆装，sloop 指单桅帆船。
hints.en: Sailing terms: a cutter-rigged sloop is a small boat with one mast and a particular sail plan.

sentences: 「什么叫『卡特里格斯洛普』？」咕咕转向吉普，小声问。

hints.zh: 咕咕把 cutter-rigged sloop 听成了一个词，所以完全听不懂。
hints.en: Gub-Gub has run the two words together into one, so he cannot make any sense of it.

sentences: 「嘘！——那是说那人的船是什么样子的，」吉普说。
「别出声，行不行？」
「哦，」小猪说，「就这个？
我还以为是能喝的东西呢。」
于是医生让男孩留在餐厅跟动物们玩，自己上楼去找路过的海豚。
不一会儿，一大群海豚一路跳着、舞着穿过水面游来，正往巴西去。

hints.zh: school 这里不是「学校」，而是一大群鱼或海兽。
hints.en: School here is not a school building: it means a large group of sea animals.

hints.zh: 巴西，南美洲国家。
hints.en: Brazil, the country in South America.

sentences: 它们看见医生靠在船栏杆上，就游过来看看他过得怎么样。

quiz.question: Why did the pirates shut the boy in the little room?
options: They were going off to rob another ship
He had tried to run away from them
They wanted him to work in the rum-room

feedback.zh: 男孩说，海盗要去抢另一条船上的东西，走之前把他锁在了那间小屋里。
feedback.en: The boy explains that the pirates shut him in there when they were going off to steal things from another ship.

quiz.question: Which two things will help the Doctor know the uncle?
options: Red hair and an anchor tattooed on his arm
A white beard and a tall hat
A wooden leg and a red coat

feedback.zh: 男孩说舅舅有一头很红的头发，胳膊上还刺着一个锚——这两样最好认，也最难认错。
feedback.en: The boy says his uncle had very red hair and a picture of an anchor tattooed on his arm — the very marks the Doctor later describes.

grammar.excerpt: the best sailor in the South Atlantic

focus.zh: best 是 good 的不规则最高级；in the South Atlantic 划出范围：整个南大西洋上没有比他更好的水手。
focus.en: Best is the irregular superlative of good; in the South Atlantic marks the group he is the best of.

introduction.zh: 医生把红头发和胳膊上的锚说给海豚听。它们说，那条船确实沉在海底，可它们还讲了别的——关于海底的甲壳类，关于海上的闲话是怎么传开的。它们究竟知不知道那个人的下落？
introduction.en: The Doctor describes the red hair and the anchor on the arm. The porpoises know the boat at once: they have seen it lying on the bottom of the sea. They also claim to hear everything that happens in the water. Is the man dead or alive?

sentences: 医生问它们有没有见过一个红头发、胳膊上刺着锚的男人。
「你说的是『俏莎莉号』的船主吗？」海豚们问。

hints.zh: 船主、船长；不是「主人」的意思。
hints.en: Master here means the owner or captain of the boat, not a servant’s master.

sentences: 「对，」医生说。
「就是他。
他是不是淹死了？」
「他的渔船沉了，」海豚们说，「因为我们看见它躺在海底。
可里面没有人，我们特意进去看过了。」
「他的小外甥就在我这条船上，」医生说。
「他非常害怕，怕海盗把他舅舅扔进了海里。
能不能请你们帮我查清楚，他到底有没有淹死？」

hints.zh: 外甥；这里指船上那个男孩，舅舅就是沉船的主人。
hints.en: Nephew: the boy on the ship, whose uncle owned the sunken boat.

hints.target: Would you be so good as to
hints.zh: 很客气的请求：「能不能劳驾你们……」
hints.en: A very polite request: “would you kindly …”

hints.zh: 确切地、肯定地。
hints.en: For sure: certainly, without any doubt.

sentences: 「哦，他没淹死，」海豚们说。
「要是他淹死了，深海的甲壳类一定会告诉我们。
海上的消息，我们全都听得到。
贝类管我们叫『海洋闲话家』。
不——告诉那小男孩，我们很遗憾不知道他舅舅在哪儿；但我们非常确定，他没有在海里淹死。」

hints.zh: 十足类动物（虾、蟹等甲壳类）；原文大写，像是海底消息最灵通的一群。
hints.en: Decapods: ten-legged sea creatures such as crabs and shrimps, here treated as a group that knows the sea’s news.

hints.zh: 「海洋闲话家」，贝类给海豚起的绰号，说它们爱传消息。
hints.en: “The Ocean Gossips”: the nickname the shell-fish give the porpoises, who carry all the news.

sentences: 于是医生带着这个消息跑下楼，告诉了那个小外甥；孩子高兴得拍起手来。
『推我拉你』把男孩驮在背上，绕着餐厅的桌子跑了一圈；其他动物都跟在后面，用勺子敲着菜盘盖子，装成一支游行队伍。

quiz.question: What did the porpoises find inside the sunken fishing-boat?
options: Nobody at all
The uncle, fast asleep
A big catch of fish

feedback.zh: 海豚说它们看见船躺在海底，还特意进去看过：里面一个人也没有。
feedback.en: The porpoises saw the sloop on the bottom of the sea and went inside to look: there was nobody there.

quiz.question: Why do the shell-fish call the porpoises “The Ocean Gossips”?
options: Because they hear and carry all the news of the sea
Because they never stop talking to ships
Because they swim from ocean to ocean

feedback.zh: 海豚说自己听得到海上所有的消息，所以贝类管它们叫「海洋闲话家」。
feedback.en: The porpoises say, “We hear all the salt-water news,” which is why the shell-fish call them The Ocean Gossips.

grammar.excerpt: If he were, we would be sure to have heard of it

focus.zh: If he were 是与眼下事实相反的假设——他并没有淹死；所以主句用 would，不用 will。
focus.en: If he were imagines something untrue now — he is not drowned — so the main clause takes would, not will.
